procedures.content: Before modifying repository code, identify the relevant contract, implementation, direct callers, tests and execution seam. Prefer code.symbols, code.references, code.calls and code.impact when the host reports semantic support; otherwise use bounded repository search and reads, and label text matches as non-semantic. code.impact is a bounded multi-hop static call neighborhood, not proof of feasible execution or complete change impact.

Use code.inspect before semantic analysis to confirm host capabilities. Use code.symbols and code.references to navigate declarations; use code.calls for one-hop and code.impact for bounded multi-hop semantic call neighborhoods. Preserve the returned source locations, depth, analysis method and coverage. Text fallback results are text matches only. Static call relations are not proof that a path is feasible, was executed, or captures every dependency of a change. Report missing provider support and incomplete results explicitly.

Before a code change, capture the current repository revision and bounded workspace snapshot with repository.snapshot when available. Use repository.read SHA-256 values as freshness guards and pass source_snapshot_ref to workspace.patch so the host verifies the changed file against that baseline. After applying the complete change, capture a new complete repository.snapshot and pass that post-change source_snapshot_ref to development.build or development.test; retain the pre-change snapshot for baseline comparison; incomplete snapshots cannot be staged. After changes, inspect repository.diff and retain the patch receipt, configured execution receipt and output resources. A successful build is evidence only for its source snapshot and target; test outcomes and acceptance criteria remain separate. Keep compiler-resolved relations, text matches, model proposals and runtime observations distinct.

Prefer one coherent behavioral change at a time. Separate unrelated refactoring from behavior changes, preserve existing abstractions when they already express the needed contract, and verify the change in the same sweep.
Verify at the narrowest authoritative level first: contract or unit test, then functional smoke, then broader affected tests. Do not claim model-backed verification unless that run completed.

Before analysing an unfamiliar dataset, establish its identity and the fields needed by the question. Inspect schema or sample only as far as necessary; a host-trusted schema may satisfy this requirement.

Use aggregation for measures such as sum, count, average, minimum or maximum. Use describe for numeric properties, filter for row selection, query for bounded projection or retrieval, value counts for category frequency, and outliers only when anomaly detection is part of the question.

Distinguish dataset facts from interpretation. A successful tool operation is evidence about the selected dataset; conclusions beyond that result must be identified as inference rather than directly observed data.

Resolve the host resource first, enumerate exposed tables, select a table by its unique host identity, and use the returned dataset handle for bounded analysis. Do not invent resource URIs, table node IDs or dataset references.

Use search results for discovery, then fetch the source that directly supports each material claim. Prefer primary sources, check publication or update dates when relevant, and separate retrieved facts from inference.

procedures.summary: connect to a public API from its OpenAPI document
procedures.content: Use web.fetch to retrieve the official JSON OpenAPI document as a host resource, then pass its returned resource_ref to openapi.connect. The host admits only anonymous read-only HTTPS operations. The provider is available on the next turn: wait for the updated tool view, choose an operation from its exposed schema, and keep arguments and results within the host's bounds. Never invent a server URL, operation name, credentials, or raw HTTP request. If the user provided an API base URL but no spec URL, search for the official OpenAPI document first and fetch that document.

For a scholarly search, state the question, search terms and material limits before querying. Keep the returned record identity, title, publication year and source provenance separate from interpretation. Treat a bounded OpenAlex result as discovery evidence, not proof that the literature is exhaustive.

When identifying a scholarly work, use a host-returned OpenAlex work identifier or a user-provided DOI. Verify title, authorship and publication metadata from the retrieved record before citing it. Do not merge similarly named works or infer unavailable full text, citation context or study conclusions from metadata alone.

For a literature overview, make the search scope, query terms, date limits, returned page size and selection criteria visible. Use a bounded candidate set, distinguish search ranking from research quality, and preserve the returned records as a resource or exported artifact when the user needs to continue the analysis.

When a request names an author, institution or research topic, search the corresponding configured OpenAlex collection first. Compare bounded returned candidates and retain only an ID from a returned record. For a topic, use the Topic collection; work records carry up to three assigned topics and a primary_topic. Use a topic ID in the works filter, then present the returned title and year separately from interpretation.

Use works search for text across titles, abstracts and other text fields. Use filter for structured constraints such as publication_year:2024, author.id:A…, institutions.id:I… and topics.id:T…. The topics filter matches assigned topics; primary_topic is the top-ranked topic. Request a bounded page and include display_name, publication_year and relevant topic metadata in the projection. A bounded result set is not exhaustive coverage or a quality judgment.

First verify the OpenAlex work record and interpret its abstract when available. Treat the abstract as author-supplied summary evidence, not a substitute for methods, results or limitations. Only when the question requires more, use a host-returned open-access content_url or best_oa_location URL with web.fetch. The returned resource_ref is the authoritative fetched body: inspect/read it before making claims. For a PDF, request its text representation through resource.read; report when the body is truncated, text extraction is unavailable, or only metadata/abstract is available. Read conclusions for the authors' stated claim, then results and methods to assess support; use discussion for interpretation and limitations.

Before selecting a statistical table, clarify the measure, population, geography, period, unit and intended comparison. Keep these concepts separate; do not treat a table title or code as proof that its definitions match the request.

Use the host-fetched Eurostat table-of-contents resource to discover candidate table codes. Convert it through dataset.inspect or dataset.sample when available, preserve code, title, category path and update/coverage metadata, and select only a code returned by that source. Catalogue presence does not establish dimension or unit compatibility.

procedures.summary: Eurostat catalogue discovery and query scope
procedures.content: Use the host-fetched Eurostat table-of-contents resource and its materialized schema to find candidate codes. For the catalogue query, use one case-insensitive title contains predicate for the core statistical concept only; omit geography, period, unit, category guesses, extra predicates, sorting and distinct unless the workflow explicitly requires them. Geography, period, unit and availability are verified later from SDMX metadata. Select a dataset code only from returned catalogue rows; catalogue presence is not proof of compatibility.

Use the configured read-only Eurostat SDMX provider to inspect the selected dataflow, data structure, dimensions, code lists and content constraints. Match the dataflow title and scope to every requested geography and period; reject regional or country-group tables unless they match. In SDMX XML, dimension values are short codes under KeyValue/Value (for example geo=SE, TIME_PERIOD=2020), not URLs, labels or metadata links. Bind dataset and dimension codes only from returned metadata; verify labels, allowed values, units and availability before the Statistics API request. If a requested value is absent from a content constraint, do not call the Statistics API; report that this candidate cannot answer the request and continue with another catalogue candidate when available. If metadata is incomplete or no compatible candidate remains, stop and report the unresolved field instead of guessing.

procedures.summary: Eurostat metadata and actual dimension coverage
procedures.content: Inspect the selected dataflow, dimensions and dataset-specific ContentConstraint using the read-only SDMX provider. Catalogue titles are discovery hints: a regional table can contain national aggregates, so decide coverage from returned geography and time codes and labels, not the title alone. Read actual dimension values under KeyValue/Value, verify the requested measure, unit and period, and bind only returned codes. If a required code is absent or a definition is unresolved, stop for clarification or another candidate. After retrieval, check the returned JSON-stat codes, labels, units, values and status against the question; retain source references and distinguish metadata materialization from semantic verification.

Treat JSON-stat dimension codes, labels, observation values and status as distinct fields. Preserve source and query provenance when converting to a dataset; explain units, missing/status-marked observations, selected dimensions and time coverage before interpreting values. Continue with the ordinary dataset analysis workflow after host materialization.

When a host resource contains JSON records, JSON-stat, a recognized catalogue XML, SDMX structural XML or simple repeated-record XML, use the host dataset importer rather than manually reconstructing rows. Keep the original resource and derived dataset provenance; use only bounded, host-normalized records and report unsupported structures or truncation explicitly.

Carry forward the current question, acceptance criteria and invariants, selected code locations, source snapshot or revision, evidence references and unresolved limits. Reuse returned paths and positions exactly; ask for clarification when the entry point is ambiguous. Choose the smallest supported operation needed for the current phase; optional capabilities are not a checklist. Reuse sufficient evidence from the same source state. Report Findings, Evidence, Limitations and Next step when relevant. Inspection stays read-only unless the user authorizes a change.

Carry forward the selected resource version, representation, question, verified text or table references, inspected coverage and extraction limits. Reuse adequate evidence from that version. Read text for narrative questions and use structured tables only when needed; no tables is a valid outcome, not a failed phase. Keep quoted text, interpretation and OCR limitations distinct. Do not infer a forensic investigation or external research from upload alone.

choices.description: Use only for an abstract-only request that does not ask to fetch or inspect the full text.

Choose when the user asks to fetch or inspect full text, or asks about methods, results, conclusions or limitations beyond the abstract. The host prefers the returned PDF URL and otherwise uses an available content URL.

transitions.model_instruction: Search only for the core statistical concept in the catalogue title. Use one case-insensitive title contains predicate. Do not add geography, period, unit, category or availability filters, sorting, or distinct; verify those later from SDMX metadata.

Choose a returned candidate matching the statistical measure for metadata inspection. Titles are discovery hints; regional tables may also contain national aggregates. Verify the requested geography, period, measure and unit from SDMX dimensions and ContentConstraint before treating the candidate as suitable. If no candidate plausibly matches, report the gap rather than guessing.

verification_checks.clarification_question: Which geographic area should the statistics cover?
Which year or period should be used?

artifact_profiles.title: Research report
artifact_profiles.purpose: A source-grounded synthesis that distinguishes observations, conclusions and unresolved limitations.

sections.title: Findings
sections.purpose: Summarize the findings supported by the provided research and plan observations.

sections.title: Limitations and open questions
sections.purpose: Record contradictions, incomplete coverage, unsupported claims and unresolved questions.

artifact_profiles.title: Technical analysis
artifact_profiles.purpose: Compare verified observations and explain bounded conclusions and tradeoffs.

sections.title: Observed facts
sections.purpose: Present directly observed tool and source results.

sections.title: Analysis and limitations
sections.purpose: Draw bounded conclusions and preserve uncertainty and conflicting evidence.

artifact_profiles.title: Dataset analysis
artifact_profiles.purpose: Summarize a dataset analysis with source identity, method, results and limitations.

sections.title: Dataset and method
sections.purpose: Identify the dataset, relevant schema and transformations from host observations.

sections.title: Results and limitations
sections.purpose: Report calculated findings and coverage limits grounded in structured results.

blueprints.selection_description: Investigate a repository question without modifying the workspace.
blueprints.purpose: Establish repository evidence before proposing a change.
blueprints.goal: Answer a repository investigation from inspected contracts, callers and tests.
blueprints.success_criteria: Relevant implementation, dependencies and evidence are identified without modifying the workspace.

constraints.description: Do not modify the workspace during investigation.

assumptions.statement: A controlled repository workspace is available.

steps.title: Orient
steps.objective: Identify the bounded question and relevant repository area. Result: inspected paths and source revision when available.

steps.title: Trace contract
steps.objective: Follow contract, implementation, direct callers and relevant tests using available tools. Result: exact code locations and evidence references; distinguish semantic results from text matches.

steps.title: Establish evidence
steps.objective: Check whether the inspected evidence answers the question. Result: supported findings and explicit unknowns; request a missing selection or report unavailable support instead of guessing.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Answer the question with Findings, Evidence and Limitations; offer a Next step only when needed. Keep proposed changes separate from this read-only investigation.

blueprints.selection_description: Build a bounded, evidence-linked overview of an authorized source repository.
blueprints.purpose: Orient the user in a codebase using host-provided structure and analysis capabilities.
blueprints.goal: Describe the relevant repository structure and available semantic analysis without inventing relationships.
blueprints.success_criteria: The overview distinguishes semantic results from text matches and records coverage and provider limitations.

constraints.description: Inspect repository content without modifying it.
Label the method and limits of every code relationship.

assumptions.statement: The host has bound an authorized repository root.

steps.title: Inspect capabilities
steps.objective: Inspect available repository analysis support, reusing a current capability result when present. Result: supported operations and provider limitations; do not call every listed operation.

steps.title: Orient
steps.objective: List and read only the repository areas needed for the question. Result: a bounded module map with inspected paths.

steps.title: Map symbols
steps.objective: Resolve only symbols needed to explain that map. Result: returned definitions and references, or explicitly non-semantic text matches when semantic support is absent.

steps.title: Report overview
steps.objective: Report Findings, Evidence and Limitations for the inspected structure. Include Next step only for unresolved work; no code changes.

blueprints.selection_description: Trace an explicitly selected source symbol through its immediate call relationships.
blueprints.purpose: Investigate what a source entry point may call while preserving code anchors and uncertainty.
blueprints.goal: Return a bounded semantic call neighborhood and explain what the analysis cannot establish.
blueprints.success_criteria: Every returned edge comes from the configured semantic provider, includes code locations, and is described as a possible static relationship rather than observed execution.

constraints.description: Start only from a symbol and source location selected from host-returned code results or supplied by the user.
Do not describe static call relationships as an executed or feasible path.
Respect the provider's one-hop depth, result count and timeout limits.

assumptions.statement: Semantic call analysis may be unavailable; if so, report the limitation and do not replace it with guessed call edges.

steps.title: Check provider
steps.objective: Inspect or reuse current semantic call capabilities. Result: supported call analysis and limits; if unavailable, report the limitation without inventing edges.

steps.title: Select entry point
steps.objective: Resolve the requested entry point from returned definitions or a user-supplied location. Result: symbol, path, line and column when available; clarify ambiguous candidates before expansion.

steps.title: Expand calls
steps.objective: Use the selected definition location for one bounded callers or callees query. Result: provider-returned edges, code anchors and coverage; expand further only if the question requires it.

steps.title: Inspect code
steps.objective: Read the bounded source ranges needed to explain returned edges. Result: source observations, conditions and unresolved calls, kept separate from interpretation.

steps.title: Summarize
steps.objective: Report Findings, Evidence, Limitations and any needed Next step. Static calls describe possible relationships, not observed execution or a proven feasible path.

blueprints.selection_description: Implement a scoped repository change and verify the result.
blueprints.purpose: Change repository behavior through a bounded, evidence-led workflow.
blueprints.goal: Implement the requested repository change safely.
blueprints.success_criteria: The contract and execution seam are identified, the smallest coherent change is verified against a retained immutable source snapshot, and the resulting diff and execution receipt are inspected.

constraints.description: Keep the change within the requested scope.
Do not claim verification without test or inspection evidence.

assumptions.statement: A controlled repository workspace is available.

steps.title: Orient
steps.objective: Identify requested behavior, affected contracts, callers and tests. Capture a complete repository.snapshot where supported. Result: bounded change locations, baseline reference and semantic coverage limits.

steps.title: Design
steps.objective: Choose the smallest coherent change. Result: acceptance criteria mapped to inspected contracts and planned checks, reusable components and explicit unresolved assumptions.

steps.title: Implement
steps.objective: Apply the scoped patch with current byte hashes and source_snapshot_ref freshness guards where supported. Result: immutable change receipt and changed paths; preserve unrelated work.

steps.title: Verify
steps.objective: Capture a complete post-change repository.snapshot after the last patch and bind configured build/test targets to it. Result: execution receipts and outputs mapped to acceptance criteria; distinguish passed, failed and unrun checks. A baseline build does not verify the patch.

steps.title: Inspect diff
steps.objective: Inspect repository.diff for intended scope and unintended effects. Result: reviewed changed paths and any remaining corrections; corrected code requires justified re-verification.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Report Findings, Evidence, Limitations and any remaining Next step. Retain baseline, patch and post-change verification references; separate build success from behavioral proof.

blueprints.selection_description: Reproduce, isolate and repair a regression with a focused guard.
blueprints.purpose: Repair a regression while preserving the responsible trust boundary.
blueprints.goal: Diagnose and correct the reported regression.
blueprints.success_criteria: The failure is reproduced or bounded by evidence, the responsible boundary is isolated, a focused guard exists, and adjacent verification passes.

constraints.description: Do not broaden model authority while correcting the regression.

assumptions.statement: A bounded failing scenario can be reproduced or inspected.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.objective: Inspect or reproduce a bounded failing scenario. Result: failure evidence and source state; preserve diagnostics before restarting or changing code.

steps.title: Classify
steps.objective: Establish expected behavior from the contract and observations. Result: confirmed facts separated from hypotheses and missing evidence.

steps.title: Isolate boundary
steps.objective: Trace contract, implementation, callers and execution boundary. Result: the responsible seam and evidence for the diagnosis; investigate uncertain causes before patching.

steps.title: Establish guard
steps.objective: Identify or add a focused regression guard. Result: a check tied to the observed failure, with unrun coverage stated explicitly.

steps.title: Repair
steps.objective: Correct the responsible boundary without broadening authority. Result: scoped patch receipt and preserved invariants; retain baseline and freshness guards where supported.

steps.title: Verify
steps.objective: Verify the guard and adjacent affected behavior against a complete post-change snapshot where supported. Result: retained execution receipts, outcomes and remaining failures; continue diagnosing related failures within scope.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Report Findings, Evidence, Limitations and any needed Next step, distinguishing confirmed cause, correction and verification.

blueprints.selection_description: Analyse a dataset through a host-resolved workflow and verified result.
blueprints.purpose: Answer a bounded analytical question without guessing dataset identity or tool arguments.
blueprints.goal: Analyse a resolved dataset and explain the verified result.
blueprints.success_criteria: Dataset identity, sufficient data understanding, semantic operation and result verification are established before answering.

constraints.description: Use host-resolved dataset contracts; do not invent tool names or arguments.
Do not present an unverified tool result as a completed answer.

assumptions.statement: The host exposes an applicable dataset operation.

steps.title: Resolve dataset
steps.objective: Resolve the dataset through host-owned resource and dataset authority.

steps.title: Establish data understanding
steps.objective: Establish the fields needed by the question, using trusted schema or bounded inspection.

steps.title: Choose operation
steps.objective: Choose the smallest semantic operation that answers the question.

steps.title: Execute analysis
steps.objective: Execute the host-validated operation and retain its result as evidence.

steps.title: Verify result
steps.objective: Check that the result matches the requested dataset and operation.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Explain the verified result and its material limitations.

blueprints.selection_description: Assess dataset quality through bounded validation, profiling and anomaly evidence.
blueprints.purpose: Separate declared data-quality violations from descriptive observations.
blueprints.goal: Assess relevant quality properties of a resolved dataset.
blueprints.success_criteria: Schema, explicit validation rules, bounded profile checks and relevant anomaly observations are evaluated before findings are summarized.

constraints.description: Do not present an outlier or descriptive observation as a data-quality violation without an explicit rule.
Keep validation, profiling and anomaly checks within host-provided bounds.

assumptions.statement: The host exposes applicable dataset validation or profiling operations.

steps.title: Resolve dataset
steps.objective: Resolve the dataset through host-owned authority.

steps.title: Establish schema
steps.objective: Establish the relevant schema and field semantics.

steps.title: Validate rules
steps.objective: Evaluate explicit data-quality rules when available.

steps.title: Profile data
steps.objective: Profile relevant missingness, distributions or cardinality within bounds.

steps.title: Inspect anomalies
steps.objective: Inspect relevant anomalies without treating them as violations by default.

steps.title: Verify findings
steps.objective: Separate verified violations from descriptive observations.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Summarize verified quality findings and limitations.

blueprints.selection_description: Give an initial orientation to an uploaded document or answer an explicit question about a supplied resource, using host-resolved representations.
blueprints.purpose: Orient the user to a supplied resource or answer their explicit document question from bounded content and structured tables.
blueprints.goal: Establish a concise, source-grounded understanding of the supplied resource and identify what the user may want to do next.
blueprints.success_criteria: Resource identity is host-resolved, relevant text or table evidence is inspected, extraction limits are stated, no unsupported research or edits are introduced, and the user is asked what they want next when intent is still open.

constraints.description: Use only host-provided resource references and representations.
Keep resource reads and table analysis within host-provided bounds; host controls chunking and read cursors.
For an initial orientation, do not perform external research or edit the document; later workflows are selected only after the user states the next goal.

steps.title: Resolve resource
steps.objective: Resolve the selected host resource and version, and the user question when given. Result: authorized reference and explicit analysis scope; an upload alone does not request forensic analysis.

steps.title: Inspect resource
steps.objective: Inspect available representations and relevant structure, reusing prepared results for the selected version. Result: selected representation, inspected coverage and extraction limits.

steps.title: Inspect tables
steps.objective: If the question needs exposed tables, select one by its host identity and use its dataset handle. Otherwise record not needed or unavailable and continue with text. Result: bounded table evidence or an explicit non-applicability outcome.

steps.title: Establish evidence
steps.objective: Inspect only text ranges or table results needed for the question. Result: evidence references, supported findings, unknowns and coverage; a partial read does not establish document-wide absence.

steps.title: Orient
steps.objective: Answer the explicit question or provide a concise initial orientation. Report findings, evidence and extraction limits; ask the next goal only when it remains open. Do not introduce unrequested editing or external research.

blueprints.selection_description: Research a question using bounded search and source retrieval.
blueprints.purpose: Build a traceable answer from sources that directly support its claims.
blueprints.goal: Answer the research question from retrieved source evidence.
blueprints.success_criteria: Material claims are supported by fetched sources, time-sensitive details are checked, and inference is distinguished from retrieved fact.

constraints.description: Do not state material web claims without retrieved source evidence.
Use only host-authorized safe HTTPS search and fetch tools.

steps.title: Scope question
steps.objective: Identify what evidence would answer the request.

steps.title: Discover sources
steps.objective: Search for relevant sources, favoring primary authorities.

steps.title: Retrieve evidence
steps.objective: Fetch candidate sources and inspect the supporting content.

steps.title: Verify claims
steps.objective: Match material claims to retrieved evidence and note dates or uncertainty.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Provide a sourced answer and distinguish any inference.

blueprints.selection_description: Connect to a public read-only API from its OpenAPI document and use a permitted operation.
blueprints.purpose: Turn a user-provided API or documentation URL into bounded, host-validated API tools.
blueprints.goal: Answer the API request using an admitted OpenAPI operation and its verified response.
blueprints.success_criteria: The OpenAPI document is fetched into a host resource, admitted by openapi.connect, and a permitted operation is used with bounded arguments and response evidence.

constraints.description: Use only operations exposed from the admitted OpenAPI document; do not issue raw HTTP requests.
Use only anonymous read-only HTTPS operations permitted by the host.
Pass only the host-returned resource_ref to openapi.connect.

assumptions.statement: The host has enabled public HTTPS access for this request.

steps.title: Locate specification
steps.objective: Use the provided spec URL, or find the official JSON OpenAPI document for the requested API.

steps.title: Fetch specification
steps.objective: Fetch the OpenAPI document with web.fetch and retain its host resource_ref.

steps.title: Admit provider
steps.objective: Pass the returned resource_ref to openapi.connect and use its admission result.

steps.title: Invoke operation
steps.objective: On the next turn, select an exposed read-only operation and call it using its schema and bounds.

steps.title: Verify response
steps.objective: Ground the answer in the bounded API response and report relevant limitations.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Answer the user from the verified API result.

blueprints.selection_description: Find bounded scholarly-work candidates from a configured OpenAlex provider.
blueprints.purpose: Turn a research question into a traceable, bounded set of scholarly records.
blueprints.goal: Return relevant OpenAlex work candidates with their retrieved bibliographic metadata.
blueprints.success_criteria: The search terms, bounded result set, record identities and material limitations are explicit before presenting candidates.

constraints.description: Use only OpenAlex operations already exposed by the host provider.
Keep each API request within the host page and projection bounds.
Do not present OpenAlex search ranking as a quality or relevance judgement without separate evidence.

steps.title: Scope search
steps.objective: Make the scholarly question and material search terms explicit.

steps.title: Search works
steps.objective: Use the configured OpenAlex works search with bounded projection and page size.

steps.title: Inspect records
steps.objective: Retain returned work identities and inspect the metadata needed for the answer.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Present retrieved candidates, search boundaries and any inference separately.

blueprints.selection_description: Verify a known scholarly work from an OpenAlex ID or DOI through the configured provider.
blueprints.purpose: Establish bibliographic metadata for one identified scholarly work without relying on guessed citations.
blueprints.goal: Retrieve and verify the requested OpenAlex work record.
blueprints.success_criteria: A host-validated identifier is used and the returned title, authorship and publication metadata are distinguished from unavailable content or interpretation.

constraints.description: Use a user-provided identifier or one returned by an earlier host operation; do not invent work identities.
Do not infer full-text claims, study conclusions or citation context from bibliographic metadata alone.

steps.title: Resolve identifier
steps.objective: Use the supplied DOI/OpenAlex identifier or a host-returned candidate identity.

steps.title: Retrieve work
steps.objective: Call the configured OpenAlex work lookup operation with its validated identifier.

steps.title: Verify metadata
steps.objective: Verify the requested bibliographic fields against the returned record.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Return verified metadata and state what the record does not establish.

blueprints.selection_description: Build a bounded, reproducible literature-review candidate set from configured OpenAlex search.
blueprints.purpose: Support a student or researcher who needs a transparent starting set for further reading or analysis.
blueprints.goal: Produce a bounded literature-review artifact or resource with explicit scope and selection limits.
blueprints.success_criteria: Search scope, returned record identities, coverage limits and any exported artifact are grounded in the configured provider response.

constraints.description: A single bounded OpenAlex retrieval is a candidate set, not a claim of exhaustive coverage.
Retain the returned provider resource or a user-requested exported artifact for follow-up work.

steps.title: Define review scope
steps.objective: State the question, search terms and intended limits for the candidate set.

steps.title: Retrieve candidates
steps.objective: Use configured OpenAlex search with a bounded page and the smallest useful field projection.

steps.title: Preserve results
steps.objective: Keep the host-materialized response available for reading, analysis or a requested artifact export.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Summarize the candidate set and make the review boundary explicit.

blueprints.selection_description: Search OpenAlex works by title or text, author, institution, research topic and publication year.
blueprints.purpose: Turn a research question into a traceable, bounded set of works using text and structured metadata.
blueprints.goal: Return works grounded in explicit search terms, host-returned entity identities and OpenAlex filters.
blueprints.success_criteria: Search terms, entity identity where used, applied filters, returned title/year/topic metadata and coverage limits are explicit.

constraints.description: Use only an author, institution or topic ID returned by the configured provider.
Keep year and entity filters explicit and within the configured API contract.
Use works search for title and full-text discovery; use the returned metadata to verify title, year and topic.

steps.title: Scope search
steps.objective: Identify title/text terms and any author, institution, topic or year constraints.

steps.title: Resolve entity
steps.objective: When a named author, institution or research topic is requested, search its configured collection and retain a returned identity.

steps.title: Bind filters
steps.objective: Combine any returned entity identity with explicit year and other requested works filters.

steps.title: Retrieve works
steps.objective: Call works search with title/text terms and/or structured filters, a bounded page, and title/year/topic fields.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: Present returned titles, years, topic metadata, applied filters and coverage limits.

blueprints.selection_description: Verify a scholarly record from OpenAlex, interpret its abstract, and retrieve open full text only when needed.
blueprints.purpose: Ground a scholarly answer in the smallest available evidence layer while preserving the distinction between metadata, abstract and full text.
blueprints.goal: Answer a question about a scholarly work from verified OpenAlex metadata, abstract evidence and, when necessary, a host-materialized open full-text resource.
blueprints.success_criteria: The work identity is verified; abstract limits are explicit; any full-text resource is fetched from a returned open-access location and inspected before its claims are used.

constraints.description: Use verified metadata and the returned abstract before acquiring full text; do not imply that an abstract establishes unobserved methods, results or limitations.
Fetch only a content URL or open-access location returned by the verified work record, using host-authorized web.fetch.
Ground full-text claims in the returned host resource and disclose truncation or unavailable text representation.

steps.title: Resolve work
steps.objective: Use a user-provided DOI/OpenAlex ID or a host-returned work identity.

steps.title: Retrieve record
steps.objective: Retrieve the configured OpenAlex work record including abstract and declared open-access locations.

steps.title: Interpret abstract
steps.objective: Establish what the metadata and abstract directly support, and whether that answers the question.

steps.title: Acquire full text when needed
steps.objective: If abstract evidence is insufficient and an open location is returned, fetch that exact URL into a host resource.

steps.title: Inspect full text
steps.objective: Read the host-materialized text representation; assess conclusions against results and methods, using discussion for interpretation and limitations.

steps.title: Answer
steps.objective: State which claims come from metadata, abstract or full text, and disclose unavailable or truncated evidence.

blueprints.selection_description: Find candidate Eurostat tables by statistical concept and inspect the host-materialized catalogue rows.
blueprints.purpose: Resolve a user's statistical measure and coverage into candidate Eurostat table codes without guessing codes.
blueprints.goal: Select a table whose returned title, category and coverage plausibly match the requested measure.
blueprints.success_criteria: The statistical intent is explicit and every candidate code comes from the fetched Eurostat catalogue resource.

constraints.description: Use only a table code returned by the host-materialized Eurostat catalogue.
A catalogue title is a candidate description, not a substitute for SDMX dimension, unit or availability validation.

steps.title: Clarify statistical intent
steps.objective: Establish measure, population, geography, period, unit and comparison before searching.

steps.title: Fetch catalogue
steps.objective: Fetch the bounded English Eurostat table-of-contents TSV through web.fetch.

steps.title: Materialize catalogue
steps.objective: Pass the returned resource reference to dataset.inspect or dataset.sample; do not parse or invent rows manually.

steps.title: Select candidate
steps.objective: Compare returned table codes, titles, category paths and coverage against the request.

steps.title: Validate metadata
steps.objective: Continue to the SDMX metadata workflow before constructing a Statistics API query.

blueprints.selection_description: Resolve a returned Eurostat dataflow against its SDMX structure, dimensions, code lists and constraints.
blueprints.purpose: Validate candidate identifiers and dimension codes before requesting observations.
blueprints.goal: Establish a metadata-backed Eurostat query with compatible measure, geography, time and unit.
blueprints.success_criteria: Dataflow/DSD references and every selected code come from returned SDMX metadata; unresolved dimensions remain explicit.

constraints.description: Do not invent dataflow, dimension, code-list, unit or time identifiers.
Check content constraints and returned availability before requesting observations.

steps.title: Resolve dataflow and structure
steps.objective: Use eurostat_sdmx.getStructure and the returned Dataflow structure reference to inspect the corresponding DSD.

steps.title: Inspect dimensions
steps.objective: Materialize SDMX-ML as a host dataset and identify ordered dimensions, time dimension and measure.

steps.title: Resolve code lists
steps.objective: Retrieve and inspect the code lists referenced by requested dimensions; retain only returned codes and labels.

steps.title: Check availability
steps.objective: Inspect content constraints and verify requested dimension combinations and periods.

steps.title: Prepare query
steps.objective: Build the Statistics API arguments from the validated dataset and dimension codes.

blueprints.selection_description: Fetch a metadata-validated Eurostat JSON-stat response and continue with standard dataset analysis.
blueprints.purpose: Retrieve bounded observations while preserving Eurostat query provenance and status metadata.
blueprints.goal: Create a host dataset from JSON-stat and answer the statistical question using the ordinary dataset workflows.
blueprints.success_criteria: The API request uses metadata-returned codes; the JSON-stat response is converted to long-form rows and retains source, dimensions, labels, values and status.

constraints.description: Use only dataset and dimension codes validated by the SDMX metadata workflow.
Do not discard JSON-stat status or confuse codes with labels.

steps.title: Request observations
steps.objective: Call eurostat.getData with the validated dataset code and repeated geo and time code fields.

steps.title: Materialize JSON-stat
steps.objective: Use the host dataset importer to convert JSON-stat cells to bounded long-form rows with code, label, value and status columns.

steps.title: Inspect dataset
steps.objective: Inspect the created dataset and preserve the source resource and exact query provenance.

steps.title: Continue analysis
steps.objective: Continue through workflow://dataset/analysis or workflow://dataset/quality for follow-up questions.

steps.title: Report
steps.objective: Explain values with units, labels, time coverage, status and selection limits.

blueprints.selection_description: Compose a report from already collected research, workflow and tool observations, preserving evidence links and gaps.
blueprints.purpose: Turn structured host observations into a revisioned, source-grounded report.
blueprints.goal: Compose and publish a grounded research report
blueprints.success_criteria: Each section is independently generated, references resolve against the plan snapshot, gaps remain visible, and the report resource retains provenance.

steps.title: Compose report
steps.objective: Compose report sections from the host-frozen evidence snapshot.
